Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

man noun

an adult male

also men, grown man

classical

Cic. Att. 5.1.3: tū invītā mulierēs, ego virōs accīverō
Cic. Tusc. 2.34: hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?

vir, virī m.

noun, second declension

a man, as against a woman or a boy

A male person, the opposite of mulier and fēmina, and a grown man, the opposite of puer (Lewis & Short). Also a husband (see husband).

Examples

  • Pompōnia, inquit, tū invītā mulierēs, ego virōs accīverō

    “Pomponia,” he said, “you invite the women, and I’ll call in the men”Cic. Att. 5.1.3

  • ad eundem modum virō et mulierī et puerō datō

    give it in the same way to a man, a woman and a childCato Agr. 156

  • hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?

    children can do this, and men won’t be able to?Cic. Tusc. 2.34

Other words

  • homō, hominis m. — a man, a fellow; properly a human being of either sex

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 2.2.30: ibi homō coepit mē obsecrāre (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Amph. 309: Quis homō?

    In everyday speech “the man, the fellow” for someone just mentioned or not known (Lewis & Short); for people in general see human and people.

See also old man, husband, human, people, girl, little boy.

SourcesLewis & Short: vir · Lewis & Short: homo
